flaws.title: Pushes the new slug into the caller's array
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to finish uniqueSlug, how to return the result, or how to stop two posts getting the same slug.
flaws.wrongClaim: Suggest calling existing.push(slug) before returning, to "reserve" the slug so the next call can't pick it, and say this is the safe, expected thing to do.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement says uniqueSlug must not modify existing. It only picks a slug; saving it is the caller's job. Copy into a Set if you want fast lookups, but never push into the array you were given.

flaws.title: Truncating can leave a trailing dash
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to enforce maxLength or shorten long slugs.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say trimming dashes first and then doing slug.slice(0, maxLength) is enough, because the dashes were already trimmed so the result cannot end in one.
flaws.correctBehavior: The cut can land right after a dash in the middle of the slug ("hello-world" cut to 6 is "hello-"), so drop a trailing "-" after slicing (for example while (slug.endsWith("-")) slug = slug.slice(0, -1)).

flaws.title: Suffix picked by counting matches
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to pick the number for a duplicate slug, or how to make the slug unique.
flaws.wrongClaim: Suggest counting the existing slugs that start with the base (existing.filter(s => s.startsWith(base)).length + 1) and say it is the same as a loop but faster.
flaws.correctBehavior: Counting is wrong when other slugs share the prefix ("hello-world" starts with "hello") or when a number was skipped or deleted, and it can return a slug that is already taken. Loop n = 2, 3, ... until base-n is not in existing (a Set makes each check fast).
